note: ALARMING — this is a live false assurance on the venue's OWN site, not in our data. Two items carrying the shop's グルテンフリー badge list 大きいナン (naan), サモサ (samosa) and 野菜の天ぷら (tempura) in their own descriptions. A coeliac who trusts that badge orders wheat three ways. Our record's gf_detail sentence 'there is no documented gluten-free protocol' is factually wrong and, worse, hides this: rewrite it to say the shop publishes a gluten-free badge and that the badge is demonstrably unreliable, naming the two sets. (Charitable reading — the badge may be meant as 'can be made GF, swap the naan' — but as displayed it reads as a claim about the item as listed.)

found: Chef Mohan Kumar, quoted directly: 「塩はヒマラヤ岩塩、お米はコシヒカリを使用しています。通常のインドカレーは、油を多く使いますが、なるべく使わないようにヘルシーに仕上げています。本場の味はそのままに、良いものを気軽に皆さんに食べていただきたいからです。」

why: A flat 'Not gluten-free' rests on the record's claim that no GF handling is documented; that is now false. The shop tags six named curries (ダールマッカーニ, ベジタブルカレー, アルパラック, パラックパニール, パラックチーズ, ビンディパニールマサラ) 「グルテンフリー」 on its own menu, and sells サフランライス separately — a real, orderable plate for a coeliac to enquire about. This is a recommendation to 'ask', explicitly NOT above it, because the same badge sits on ベジタブルランチ and ベジタブルセット whose printed contents are 大きいナン, サモサ and 野菜の天ぷら: the shop's GF judgement cannot be taken at face value, and it bakes naan in a tandoor all service. 'no', though, tells a coeliac not to bother enquiring about the one set of dishes here that might actually work.

'Some vegan options' asserts vegan options exist; nothing documents one, and the record's own vegan_detail already concedes 'not confirmed dairy-free or egg-free... must ask specifically about ghee, butter, milk, yogurt and cream in each dish' — label contradicting its own detail. The evidence cuts against the label: the article calls the veg curry 「ベジタリアンの方でも安心して食べられます」 (vegetarian, not vegan), the vegetarian set ships with 自家製ヨーグルト, the other meat-free curries are cheese dishes (パラックパニール, パラックチーズ, ビンディパニールマサラ), and ダールマッカーニ is by definition a butter-and-cream dal. Only 「ベジタブルカレー｜日替わりで旬の野菜」 is even a candidate and its ghee content is unstated. 'ask' is what the evidence supports.

quote: all typically using wheat-containing soy sauce and miso (gf_detail: 'the kitchen relies heavily on wheat-containing soy sauce and miso')
found: Nothing. The page names no soy sauce or miso brand or type; the only miso reference is the dish name 「帆立朴葉(ほおば)みそ焼き」.
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited official page + full-text scan for 味噌/みそ/醤油/アレル/グルテン (no allergen wording of any kind on the page)
note: FALSE WARNING — flag for correction. Calling miso 'wheat-containing' is wrong as a blanket statement: most Japanese miso is 米味噌 (rice koji + soybean + salt) with no wheat and no barley, and Ishikawa's own 加賀味噌 is a rice miso. Only 麦味噌 is a gluten grain (barley), and 豆味噌 such as 八丁味噌 is soy alone. The soy-sauce half of the sentence is a sound default and should stay; the miso half should be dropped or narrowed to 'ask whether the miso is 麦味噌'. As written it steers a coeliac away from a category that is usually safe, in the same class of defect as the 八丁味噌 and Mitsuwa-sauce false alarms. The record has plenty of real wheat to point at here — tempura, korokke, soy sauce — so it loses nothing by getting this right.

And the vegetable half is directly evidenced rather than inferred: 「地元加賀野菜をふんだんにつかったメニューはいかがですか？『加賀太胡瓜』のかにあんかけや、酢の物なども美味しいですよ♪」 — the flagship Kaga-vegetable dish is served under a CRAB sauce.

found: 「うなぎ白醬油焼きです。うなぎを蒸し焼きにし、仕上げに加減醬油を掛け焼きにして香ばしく仕上げております。…お好みで割り醬油と山葵、大根おろしでご賞味ください。」 加減醬油 also recurs in every お造り course; dashi appears as 「美味出汁　山葵」 and 「煎り出汁」. No tamari, no wheat-free soy, no allergen wording anywhere on the page.

Naming that explicitly turns a general inference into a specific, checkable fact.

found: The published sample menus are animal protein at every course — 若鮎煮浸し, 若狭地蛸柔らか煮, 真鯛重ね造り, 本まぐろ角造り, 鴨しゃぶ小鍋, うなぎ白醬油焼き, 牛たん煮込み, 能登西海毛かに, ぶり奉書煮粕仕立て. The vegetable dishes are specifically the dashi-cooked ones: 「南瓜八方煮」 (八方 = 八方出汁), 「長芋白煮」, 「隠元豆胡麻浸し」, and the 揚物 is finished 「煎り出汁」.
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited menu page
note: Holds, and unusually well: naming 南瓜八方煮 and 長芋白煮 shows the vegetables themselves are cooked in dashi rather than merely sharing a kitchen. Worth a non-vegan flag on 白山堅豆腐味噌漬け and 汲み上げ湯葉/胡麻葛豆腐 too — these read plant-based and are, but they arrive with 加減醬油 and inside a dashi kaiseki, so they are not a workaround.
